body:
This seems to be related to the fact that you're childing a `RigidBody3D` (the wheels) to another moving object (the car), which is known to cause all kinds of weird problems, since you effectively end up setting the transforms of the wheels every single frame, as a result of their parent node moving.

This is vaguely mentioned in [the documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_rigidbody3d.html) as being problematic, even for Godot Physics, although the manifestations of these problems seems to be different for different engines:

> Note: Changing the 3D transform or `linear_velocity` of a RigidBody3D very often may lead to some unpredictable behaviors.

It should really be spelled out more clearly in the documentation that you should not child a `RigidBody*D` to a constantly moving object, like another `RigidBody*D`.

A quick fix in your case is to add a script like this to your wheels:

```gdscript
extends RigidBody3D

func _ready() -> void:
    top_level = true
```

That'll allow you to keep the parent-child relationship, but the moment `_ready` gets called (i.e. when the wheels are added to the physics simulation) they become top-level nodes, which means they won't have their transform changed by their parent anymore, and will only be controlled by the joint.

You can also just restructure your nodes so that the wheels are not childed to `Car` of course.

With all that said, this of course doesn't explain the discrepancy between the extension and the built-in Jolt module, which is a bit odd, and might warrant looking into further.

Thank you very much for your help! Both of your solutions work fine with the MRP.
I wasn't aware I was doing something wrong and somehow always assumed, that only the joint would manage the position and rotation of node_b.
Thank you both - mike's solution also helped with my similar issue. +1 to a stronger warning in the documentation!

> With all that said, this of course doesn't explain the discrepancy between the extension and the built-in Jolt module, which is a bit odd, and might warrant looking into further.

I decided to do some bisecting to find out where this discrepancy came from, and it seems to have appeared as a result of #100983, which changed things around a bit, like how bodies register to have their state synchronized with the rest of the engine.

However, in a weird twist it seems I wasn't actually able to reproduce this issue on latest `master` anymore, because it turns out that #107454 somehow undid this particular discrepancy, at least within this specific MRP.

I can't make much sense of why exactly #100983 caused this change in behavior, and even less so why #107454 changed it back, but I have to assume that whatever feedback loop that's caused by continuously setting the transforms of the wheels is somehow sensitive to the order in which the bodies are added to the simulation, since that's the only thing that #107454 really could have changed.

Anyway, just to be clear, you should still not child a RigidBody3D to another moving node. That will still cause all kinds of weird problems. I'll try to make the documentation clearer instead.
